source.title: Optimization Theory for ReLU Neural Networks Trained with Normalization Layers
source.authors: Yonatan Dukler; Guido Montúfar; Quanquan Gu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves convergence of a two-layer ReLU network from random initialization under Weight Normalization, using regression loss and theoretical finite-step gradient-descent results. This bears conceptually on training convergence, but it does not measure classification error on the benchmark settings in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical convergence bounds for Weight-Normalized regression training, including linear convergence under data, initialization, width and step-size assumptions. It does not test CIFAR classification error, corrupt or random labels, or the other concrete empirical settings in V1–V6. Cited results about unnormalized networks and normalization methods are prior work, not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence results for Weight-Normalized two-layer ReLU regression. These do not test V1's convolutional classification error, V2's teacher-student minima frequencies, V4's activation-matched signal propagation, or V6's Batch Normalization effects. It reports no results on depth degradation or stability-threshold behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove conditional linear convergence for Weight-Normalized two-layer ReLU regression and derive a length-direction decomposition of the training kernel. They obtain improved sufficient-width bounds relative to earlier unnormalized analyses and argue that choosing the initialization scale can improve convergence. Proposition 2's comparison is non-strict, so it establishes an at-least-as-favorable rate rather than universal strict acceleration.
record.recipe_differences: The analysis concerns Weight-Normalized two-layer ReLU regression, not the benchmark classification recipes in the claim versions; reported results are convergence theorems rather than empirical classification runs.
record.method_sensitivity: The convergence theorem distinguishes α < 1 and α ≥ 1 regimes, with different width bounds and convergence rates; finite-step gradient descent also requires a step size tied to the evolution matrix.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.1–4.2 and B.1–B.2 establish linear convergence of sufficiently wide Weight-Normalized two-layer ReLU regression networks under stated data and initialization assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-Normalized two-layer ReLU regression converges linearly under sufficient width and suitable initialization, with additional step-size restrictions for gradient descent.

fits_no_version.finding: The initialization scale changes the convergence bounds: smaller alpha accelerates gradient flow in the V-dominated regime but requires smaller discrete steps; larger alpha reduces the sufficient width in the G-dominated regime. Proposition 2 gives an optimized-scale convergence comparison with unnormalized training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight Normalization's initialization scale controls convergence guarantees and sufficient width; an optimized scale yields a convergence-rate bound at least as favorable as unnormalized training.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 108 (2020)
record.problems: The results are theoretical sufficient-condition guarantees, not empirical tests; they concern two-layer regression, require normalized non-parallel data and bounded targets, and assume substantial over-parameterization. No classification benchmark, control experiment, or capability check is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result meeting the row criteria was omitted. Cited results in Related Work and the Introduction are prior work and were not extracted as this study's results.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional CIFAR classification error under SGD or Adam, including random labels and recipe or model-size qualifications.
All parts: teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
All parts: training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, prevention of vanishing or exploding signals and gradients, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
All parts: recovery above the initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
All parts: Batch Normalization's effects on accuracy speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: These are theoretical sufficient-condition results, not empirical observations. Improved width guarantees relative to earlier proofs do not establish that unnormalized networks actually require greater width. Proposition 2 is additional relevant context outside all six versions, so its omission does not warrant a version-linked missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error; corrupted or random labels; SGD or Adam; smaller models, early stopping and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and student-width comparisons.
Depth effects, plain versus residual networks, ImageNet/CIFAR classification, and deep tanh or normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation measurements, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain-network training.
Learning-rate thresholds, loss rises or divergence, curvature/sharpness, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch Normalization accuracy speed and learning-rate tolerance in MNIST, CIFAR-10 or ImageNet; Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network of the form (1.2), trained with Weight Normalization
rows.operation_detail: Finite-step gradient descent with Weight Normalization on square loss; theorem gives a linear prediction-error bound in the V-dominated regime.
rows.note: A theorem, not an empirical measurement; the result is for regression prediction error and holds under the stated assumptions and sufficient width.
rows.check: The theorem and bound are accurately recorded, but regression convergence with Weight Normalization measures none of V1–V6. Its guarantee cannot establish an observed effect for those versions.
